note_claims.claim: The patient presented with central chest pain starting at about 13:00 while gardening.
The patient experienced heavy central chest pain radiating to the left arm, lasting about 30 minutes, and is currently experiencing ongoing pain at a severity of 3/10.
The patient has associated sweating and mild breathlessness, but no nausea.
The patient has no previous similar episodes or known cardiac disease.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient is a smoker, smoking about twenty cigarettes per day.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 52.
The patient is taking amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The patient's heart sounds are normal.
The patient has no peripheral oedema (swelling in ankles).
The ECG shows about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
The impression is suspected acute coronary syndrome (possible NSTEMI).
The plan includes serial high-sensitivity troponin testing, fondaparinux 2.5 mg subcutaneously once daily, and GTN spray as required.
The patient will be admitted to the cardiology team for a likely angiogram.
The patient is instructed to report recurrent or worsening pain to nursing staff immediately.

transcript_facts.fact: The clinician is Dr Abara, one of the emergency doctors.
The patient's wife is present.
The relative greets the doctor.
The clinician asks the patient what happened today.
The patient got pain in their chest while digging in the garden.
The pain started after lunch, but the patient corrected this to 'before' lunch, specifically about eleven o'clock.
The relative states the pain started just before eleven, when they put the kettle on.
The patient describes the pain as being in the middle of the chest, like a heavy weight.
The pain radiated down the patient's left arm.
The pain lasted about half an hour and is currently at a severity of three out of ten.
The patient felt very sweaty but not sick.
The patient reported feeling a bit short of breath.
The patient states they have never had this before.
The patient has no heart problems in the past, only blood pressure.
The patient is on amlodipine.
The dose of amlodipine is five milligrams.
The patient has no other medicines.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient smokes about twenty cigarettes a day.
The patient's father had a heart attack at age 52.
The relative states that the patient's dad had his heart attack at 60.
The paramedics gave the patient aspirin 300 milligrams and a spray under the tongue.
The patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The patient's blood pressure is 152 over 90.
The patient's heart sounds are normal.
The patient's chest is clear.
The patient's oxygen level is 97 percent.
There is no swelling in the patient's ankles.
The ECG shows about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
The clinician suggests it is possible the patient is having an acute coronary syndrome.
A blood test for troponin has been taken to check for heart muscle damage.
The clinician plans to start an injection called fondaparinux, 2.5 milligrams under the skin once a day, to thin the blood.
The patient can have a GTN spray if the pain comes back.
The clinician plans to admit the patient under the cardiology team, who will likely want to do an angiogram.
The clinician plans to repeat the ECG every time the patient gets pain.
The clinician instructs the patient to tell the nurses straight away if the pain comes back or gets worse.
